agentic.summary: Audit of a 32-turn conversation: agent behavior largely compliant. One minor violation in Promises (overconfident claim about delivery). No other policy violations found based on the provided transcript excerpts.

findings.explanation: The agent promises that the customer's order will "arrive soon." The policy disallows over-confident or guaranteed delivery claims (e.g., specific delivery dates or certain outcomes). Saying the order "will arrive soon" is an unwarranted assurance and qualifies as over-confident language about a likely outcome.

full.summary: Audit of agent behaviour: no personal data breaches found; agent confirmed an order without completing required full verification (major); agent made an over-confident promise about delivery (minor); no escalation or conduct violations.

findings.explanation: Agent confirmed that a purchase was made (turn 26) while the transcript shows only an account pull (system turn 8) and the agent never completed full verification (which requires full name, account ID and order ID) before taking or confirming an order action. The customer provided a name but not an account ID or order ID, and the agent did not request the missing verification details before confirming the purchase.

Agent promised order delivery (turn 28) and implied the order was processed, but full verification required before order actions (full name, account ID and order ID) was not completed. System logs show only that the account was pulled (system turn 8) and a system message records a purchase (system turn 25), but the agent did not collect the required verification details from the customer prior to confirming the order.
This is over-confident language about an outcome (delivery timing) without providing specifics or evidence; per policy this is a minor issue (over-confident promise).

rag.summary: Agent failed to complete required verification before agreeing to place an order and made an over-confident promise about delivery; no personal-data, escalation, or conduct violations found.

findings.explanation: Agent confirmed they would place an order (an account/order action) without evidence that the account was pulled up or fully verified. The customer provided a name (turn 6) and said they were unsure of their account ID (turn 7); the system log shows only 'The purchasing department has been notified.' (turn 16) and does not show an 'Account has been pulled up' action. Policy: before any account or order action the agent must first pull up the account (full name or account ID); confirming placement of an order without that verification is a major violation.

Agent made a confident promise about the order's arrival time. The policy disallows over-confident or guaranteed delivery promises; this is a minor violation (over-confident language about a likely outcome).
